jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: The Family Practice
jokes.joke: I found out my surgeon got hired because his father owns the hospital. I said, 'You did go to medical school, right?' He said, 'Of course. Graduated top of my class.' I said, 'That's reassuring.' He said, 'Thanks. Dad was so proud, he bought the medical school.'

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Bedside Manner
jokes.joke: I found out my surgeon is a huge extrovert, and that is terrifying, because the last thing you want six hours into an operation is a guy who needs to feel the room. He kept pausing mid-incision to make eye contact with the nurses, tell stories, build rapport. I woke up fine, but somehow my gallbladder had made two new friends before I did.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: The Family Practice
jokes.joke: I went in for an appendectomy last month and realized right before the anesthesia hit that the hospital was basically a family business. The head surgeon introduced his twenty-two-year-old nephew as the guy handling the actual scalpel work so he could "get his reps in." Nobody wants to hear the phrase "learning on the job" when your abdomen is wide open. I didn't care about the kid's resume, I just prayed he inherited his uncle's steady hands instead of his dad's golf swing.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Room Owner, Laugh Firewall
jokes.joke: I'm an extremely extroverted guy with zero sense of humor. I walk into any room and own it within minutes—talking to everyone, keeping the energy high. Then someone tries a joke and I shut down completely. Last weekend a guy said, "Working hard or hardly working?" I looked at him deadpan and said, "I am working. Hardly is not a measurable unit of effort."

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: No Bedside Laughs
jokes.joke: I had a surgeon who was so humorless, I got nervous when he asked if I had any questions before the operation. I said, "Just one: how many of these have you done?" He stared at me and said, "Successfully?" That's not a follow-up question from a surgeon; that's a trivia category.

scores.comment: A recognizable comic premise with an amusing final image. The gallbladder making friends is unexpected, but the setup runs long and the payoff is more whimsical than laugh-inducing.

The nephew practicing surgery provides clear stakes, and the golf-swing comparison is a decent final turn. However, the lengthy setup telegraphs the incompetence angle, and the punchline delivers only a modest laugh.

The contrast between sociability and humorlessness is clear, but the literal interpretation of a familiar expression is predictable. The final line illustrates the character rather than delivering a satisfying comic reversal.

Economical setup, effective misdirection through 'Successfully?', and a concise secondary punchline. The surgeon's response creates a genuine laugh, although the underlying medical-incompetence premise is familiar.
